$comment: Read by `npm run beta:supply-chain`. Two kinds of exception, both deliberately awkward to add.
`advisories` accepts a NON-blocking production advisory. `high` and `critical` cannot be
accepted here at all — the gate fails on them regardless of what this file says. Every entry
needs an `advisory` (the GHSA id), a `reason` and an `expires`; an expired entry FAILS, so an
acceptance is a decision with a review date rather than a permanent one. An entry for an
advisory the audit no longer reports also fails, because a standing acceptance of a fixed
`advisory` is required and is checked against the GHSA the audit actually reports. It was added
on 2026-09-11 after the quill entry was found accepting `GHSA-4943-9vgg-gr5r`, a 2021 advisory
affecting quill <= 1.3.7, while 2.0.3 was installed — so the advisory that really applied had
never been reviewed, and this gate called the acceptance satisfied on every run because the
package NAME matched. Keying on the name accepts a package; keying on the id accepts a finding.
`affects` is optional, and when present must equal the audit's reported range, so an upgrade
into a newly-affected range cannot pass under a review of the old one.
`unreferencedDependencies` excuses a production dependency that no source file imports. Four
of these turned out to be genuinely unused — `openai`, `express`, `cors`, `dotenv` — and were
removed rather than listed. An entry here means the package is required by something other
than an import: the Angular runtime, or a version pin that satisfies an adf-core peer. If the
package becomes referenced, or stops being a dependency, its entry fails as unnecessary.

quill.reason: GHSA-v3m3-f69x-jf25 — XSS via Quill's HTML export, affecting quill = 2.0.3, which is what we run and is the latest published release (verified against the registry: there is nothing to upgrade to). Not reachable as configured, on both directions of travel. WRITE: note-editor.ts:502-503 reads getSemanticHTML() and passes it through DOMPurify.sanitize() before returning, and that return value is what onSave() emits and the parent persists. READ: a text/html note is rendered by note-editor.ts:118-120, the htmlReadonlyView computed, which passes the stored content through renderTrustedHtml() — that is the path a Quill-authored note actually takes back to a reader, and it is row 4 of the Category D table in docs/sonarcloud-security-remediation-plan.md. getSemanticHTML()'s only other caller, note-editor.ts:484, compares the value for equality and discards it. Each half is enforced by a different thing, and neither covers the other: the READ path by sanitizer-audit.mjs check 5, which walks the AST to require a sanitise call paired with every bypassSecurityTrustHtml; the WRITE path by note-editor.spec.ts 'sanitises the exported HTML before emitting it', which drives onSave() with hostile markup and asserts what saveNote emits. Check 5 CANNOT cover the exporter — it fires on the presence of bypassSecurityTrustHtml and readQuillHtml() has none, it returns a plain string — so before that test existed, deleting the sanitise call left every gate green while raw Quill output was persisted. Revisit on the next Quill release or when the editor is replaced.
$corrections: Re-reviewed 2026-09-11 because the previous entry was wrong in every verifiable particular while its conclusion was right — the most believable kind of stale acceptance, and one this gate cannot catch, since it matches entries by package name and never reads the GHSA or the line numbers.

It cited GHSA-4943-9vgg-gr5r, a 2021 advisory affecting quill <= 1.3.7. We run 2.0.3, so that advisory does not apply to this repository at all, and the advisory that does — GHSA-v3m3-f69x-jf25, published 2026-01-13 — was therefore accepted by accident rather than by decision.
All four source pointers were stale: document-detail.ts:1694 and :3133 are an unrelated collection check and a lock comment; note-editor.ts:89 and :95 are an imageUploading signal and an editor ref.

It named the guardrail `checkSanitizerPairing`. That was not a false claim when written, but it is now: the check was deliberately removed and superseded by sanitizer-audit.mjs check 5, which is AST-based rather than regex-based. The protection is real and stronger; only the name was wrong.

Second review pass, same day: the correction above then overstated things in its own turn, by naming check 5 as the enforcement for ALL of it. Review caught that check 5 cannot see the exporter at all, since it triggers on bypassSecurityTrustHtml and readQuillHtml() contains none. The mitigation this whole acceptance rests on had no enforcement of any kind. A test was added and confirmed to fail when the sanitise call is removed. Recorded because the failure repeated inside one file in one day: a claim about which gate covers a mitigation is as easy to get wrong as the mitigation itself, and nothing machine-checks it.

Third review pass, same day: the READ path was cited as document-detail.ts:1862 and :3394. Both sit inside `if (mime === 'text/markdown')` branches, so neither renders the text/html content Quill's export produces — the pointers named real sanitised code that is irrelevant to this advisory. The actual path is note-editor.ts:118-120. That is the FOURTH stale or wrong source pointer found in this one entry, across three reviews in a single day, and the pattern is now the point: the prose in this field carries the whole argument and nothing verifies a word of it. The `advisory` and `affects` fields were added precisely to move some of that burden onto the gate; the source pointers remain unverified by anything but a reader.

unreferencedDependencies.tslib: Emitted helper library. The TypeScript compiler generates imports of it into the build output; no source file names it.
unreferencedDependencies.@angular/animations: Required by @angular/material at runtime for its transitions. Never imported by our source.
unreferencedDependencies.@angular/material-date-fns-adapter: Version pin only. @alfresco/adf-core declares it as an unbounded `>=` peer, so without an exact pin a clean install floats it to the Angular 22 line and the build dies with `Unsupported enum value`. See docs/adf-hx-upstream-findings.md 2.1.
unreferencedDependencies.@mat-datetimepicker/core: Version pin only, and one of the two that deliberately differ from adf-core's suggestion: its major track is offset from Angular's, so 16.0.1 is correct for Angular 20.
unreferencedDependencies.date-fns: Version pin only, to keep @angular/material-date-fns-adapter and adf-core agreeing on one copy.
unreferencedDependencies.pdfjs-dist: Version pin only, and the second deliberate deviation: 4.x downgrades a shared native package, so 6.2.108 is pinned.
unreferencedDependencies.minimatch: Version pin only. Declared as a `>=10.0.0` peer by @alfresco/adf-core.
unreferencedDependencies.angular-oauth2-oidc: Version pin only. A direct dependency of @alfresco/adf-core; pinned here so a clean install cannot float it.
unreferencedDependencies.cropperjs: Version pin only. A direct dependency of @alfresco/adf-core; pinned here so a clean install cannot float it.
